units.prompt: An east-positive rail controller supplies only a velocity-time record: +3 m/s during 0–3 s, −2 m/s during 3–5 s and +1 m/s during 5–7 s. The sections are uniform-velocity intervals with ideal sharp joins. Observer B uses a reversed scale y=14−x and records y(5 s)=10 m. Independently recover x at t=0, 3, 5 and 7 s; the x-frame total displacement and distance; the three y-frame signed velocities; and the behavior exactly at the t=3 s corner. Decide whether passing x=0 implies a stop. Give a signed-area verification.

fields.label: Model selection
options: Signed-area inverse with a position anchor
Position is the speed plotted over time
One constant acceleration for all intervals

fields.label: First segment velocity in observer y frame (m/s)
Sharp-corner velocity at t=3 s
options: Unequal one-sided velocities; no unique value
Velocity is the average of +3 and −2

units.prompt: Two carts A (3 kg) and B (2 kg) touch through a light, compressed spring bumper while separating, at an instant before the bumper loses contact. The bumper transmits a repulsive force to the right on B and left on A, not a rigid linkage. On a smooth east-positive track an external motor pushes A east with 18 N and a brake pushes B west with 4 N. Sensors at that same instant read a_A=+2 m/s² and a_B=+4 m/s². Infer the bumper contact force separately from each body's equation; identify the third-law recipients and check the combined-system acceleration. Explain why different accelerations are allowed at this instant but would contradict maintained rigid contact.

fields.label: Which contact model fits the experiment?
options: Compliant unloading bumper; unequal acceleration possible
Rigid maintained contact; unequal acceleration allowed

fields.label: Force on B from A (N east)
What would maintained rigid contact require?
options: Both carts must have equal acceleration

units.prompt: In a 120 s controlled experiment, both samples receive 90 W electrical power and lose 30 W to the surroundings (assumed constant). Sample A contains both solid and liquid at its measured melting temperature throughout the interval; the latent heat of fusion is 180 kJ/kg and enough solid is initially present. Sample B stays entirely solid without transition and has total effective heat capacity 600 J/K. Compute net energy for each; infer A's melted mass and B's temperature rise; identify which energy-storage model is warranted for each; explain why A's temperature plateau does not mean it gained no energy.

fields.label: Identify the two energy-storage regimes
options: A: phase plateau; B: sensible heating

fields.label: Net energy received by either sample (J)

units.prompt: A source and microphone are stationary on the same side of a sufficiently large plane wall. Their separation parallel to the wall is b=12 m. Sound travels at 325 m/s. A microphone records the direct pulse at exactly 40.000 ms since emission and the reflected pulse at 46.154 ms since emission (rounded to 0.001 ms). Independently recover the two perpendicular wall distances if the source is farther from the wall than the microphone. Draw the virtual-source geometry, check both path lengths, and decide whether a detector requiring 7 ms separation can resolve the two pulses. State which ambiguity returns if the farther/nearer ordering is removed.

fields.label: Select the geometric reconstruction
options: Distance equals v times excess delay divided by two
The direct pulse takes the same route as the echo

fields.label: Detector result for 7 ms separation
options: Resolved: reflected arrival >7 ms since emission
